The paper was published in Advanced Materials Research Vols. 490-495 in 2012.
The standard plate is designed for the 3 mm band frequency range of 90-100 GHz.
The previous standard plate specified in national military standards was 180mm×180mm×5mm.
The existing national military standard (GJB 2038-94) only covers 8-18 GHz frequency range.
The truncated sphere design has a radius ranging from 100-500mm.
The bottom side length of the truncated sphere ranges from 50-300mm.
The thickness of the standard plate ranges from 5-20mm.
The nominal reflectivity values are -5dB, -10dB, and -15dB.
Simulation results show an uncertainty of 0.8dB in constant reflectivity.
The standard plate is made of high permittivity metal conductor.
The radar cross section formula used is σ = 4πL⁴/λ².
The reflectivity calculation uses the ratio of reflection powers: Γ = Pa/Pm.
The measurement system uses a laser model locator for alignment.
The calibration process involves two standard plates (-10dB and -5dB) for two-step verification.
The paper references a 2007 study on standard substances for 8 mm band measurements.
The standard plate has been tested and used at the authors' working place.
The new standard plate is particularly useful for bow test method and space translation method measurements.
The reference signal power (Pr) is proportional to the transmitted signal.
The paper addresses limitations of previous standards that lost function at 90-100 GHz.
The design was developed to support stealth technology advancement.
The standard plate provides reliable defined values for system calibration.
The measurement requires samples and standard plates to have the same dimensions.
Two electromagnetic waves of the same power are incident on both the sample and standard plates.
The residual error from the -5dB standard plate measurement is used to correct absorbing material measurements.
The paper emphasizes the importance of both microwave equipment calibration and integrated system adjustment.
